story.headline: Stocks edge higher, led by Health Care; small caps surge
story.lede: The S&P 500 is +0.3%, the Nasdaq -0.0%, the Dow +1.0% and the Russell 2000 +1.7%. 404 of 503 S&P 500 stocks are up. Futures point higher (+0.31%).

points.lead: Index read: S&P +0.3%, Nasdaq -0.0%, Dow +1.0%, Russell 2000 +1.7%.
points.body: Small caps are outrunning large caps. That usually means falling yields or improving growth expectations, because small companies borrow more and are more rate-sensitive.

points.lead: Sectors: Health Care leads (+2.4%), Technology lags (-0.3%).
points.body: Defensive and rate-sensitive sectors lead while small caps outperform, which fits easing yields more than a flight to safety.

EFX (Industrials, +11.3%): named in a movers roundup. HAS (Consumer Discretionary, +11.2%): named in a movers roundup. MRNA (Health Care, +6.7%): no headline in our feed yet; check the company's filings for a catalyst. GM (Consumer Discretionary, -6.8%): named in a movers roundup. Roundup: "Stocks making the biggest moves midday: Hasbro, Northrop Grumman, Equifax, General Motors & more".

points.lead: Rates, commodities and volatility: the 10-year yield is 5.12% (-2 bp); WTI crude is +1.6%; the VIX is 17.3 (-6.1%).
points.body: No large cross-asset move is driving stocks today.

data.bottom: The economic readings lean negative. 0 improved and 7 worsened in the latest releases. Readings that move prices and growth in the wrong direction at once (higher inflation with weaker hiring) are the hardest mix for the Fed and for stock valuations.

rows.why: Inflation sets the Fed's path. Faster price growth means higher-for-longer rates, which is a headwind for stock valuations.
Core strips out food and energy and shows underlying price pressure, the part the Fed can actually influence.

rows.read: The labor market is loosening (up from 4.1%).
rows.why: A rising jobless rate shows demand for workers cooling. Modest rises ease inflation; fast rises signal recession risk.
Hiring pace drives income and spending. Thin payroll growth raises recession odds even as it eases Fed pressure.
Retail sales track consumer demand, the largest part of GDP and a driver of company revenue.
Weekly layoff filings are the fastest-moving labor indicator. Sustained increases warn of a turn.
Consumer mood tends to lead spending. Low readings usually mean cautious shoppers.

watch.why: Every inflation, jobs and yield move between now and then shifts what traders expect the Fed to do.
Prediction markets price this close to a coin flip, so a surprise in the data can swing it quickly (Kalshi).

watch.e: Index levels in play: S&P 500 near its 50-day average (7,704); Nasdaq Comp. near its 50-day average (26,622); Russell 2000 near its 200-day average (2,797); Dow Jones near its 50-day average (52,389).
watch.why: Traders watch these lines for a break or a bounce; a close through one often changes the short-term trend.

wild.body: That is unusually broad participation. Moves with this many stocks up tend to reflect macro news (rates, oil, policy) more than individual company stories.
The largest one-day move in the S&P 500 today, in Industrials. Moves this size for a large company usually come from earnings, guidance or a deal.

wild.h: A 1.7-point gap between the Russell 2000 (+1.7%) and the Nasdaq (-0.0%)
wild.body: Big gaps between index groups mark rotation days, when money moves between styles instead of in or out of stocks.
Yields have sat at or above this level for months. High yields compete with stocks for money and raise borrowing costs across the economy.
